title: Write the supported scope down, and shrink it until the guarantees hold

title: Publication enforcement - a failed verification must withhold, not annotate
why: R1, the largest release-gate gap the review names. `grounded` is read once, at _orchestrator.py:5059, and decides only which memory bucket the turn is filed in. A boolean annotation is not a publication policy.
acceptance: B04: a forced numerical verification failure withholds the affected claim in text, in the chart AND in the export. B05: numbers unchanged but the rendered day, unit or room altered is blocked by semantic verification. Inspect the actual final artifacts, not the verifier flag. Honest-decline paths untouched. Start narrow: analytics, report, compare, trend.
evidence: DELIVERED 2026-09-10: orchestrator/services/publication_gate.py, called in _response_node AFTER the rewriting guards and BEFORE the message is appended; withholds text, chart (visualization_path) and export. 20 unit tests, negative cases deliberately outnumbering positive ones - honest declines, ungated lanes and identifiers-that-are-not-measurements must all pass through untouched. Two of them assert the gate is actually CALLED and correctly ordered (the V6-T10 step). export_result and publication_decision added to the per-turn stale-clear list, caught by the existing BUG-392 guard. FOUND UNDERNEATH IT, both P1: BUG-508, the verifier counted SQL rows one level too shallow and had NEVER seen a real result (fixed - analytics went sql_rows=0 -> 6960 live), and it reported 'not my lane' as 'unsupported' for 20+ intents (fixed via an `applicable` field). BUG-509, the planner writes every result into a local context never merged onto the bus, so a planner-routed turn is invisible to everything downstream (NOT fixed - belongs to V12-14). LIVE: a good report and a good analytics answer both publish; a hand-built failure withholds text, chart and export in the running process. WHY PARTIAL, stated rather than implied: (1) R1 is NOT closed for the report lane - the lane BUG-475 happened in - because BUG-509 makes it unassessable; (2) case B05, numbers right but rendered day/unit/room wrong, needs V12-08's normalised request; (3) no naturally-failing live turn has been demonstrated end-to-end, only a hand-built one. || CLOSED 2026-09-11. R1 now holds for the REPORT LANE, the lane BUG-475 happened in: report and export are back in the verifier's _ASSESSABLE_INTENTS, and the live log shows why that is now honest - '[planner] published to bus: sparql_result, sql_result, analytics_result, report_result' followed by '[verifier] grounded=True, confidence=0.88, source=analytics, sensors=2, sql_rows=1000' on the same turn. A good report publishes; the gate does not suppress it. The test now asserts BOTH halves together - that report is claimed assessable AND that the planner still publishes at both exits - because either half alone passes while the pair is broken, which is exactly the state that withheld a good report on 2026-09-10. STILL OWED, unchanged: case B05 (numbers right, rendered day/unit/room wrong) needs V12-08's normalised request.

title: Simulation governance - simulated evidence must not win an operational ranking
why: R4, and WORSE than the review assumed. 3,004 points declare simulated, ZERO declare measured, 1,342 are silent - and silence reads as measured to any default-permissive consumer. Provenance is resolved per STORE by synthetic_lookup(stored_at), a function of a table name. scorer.py contains no reference to provenance, admissibility or eligibility; it filters on Hardness only, and the flag is merely displayed in the dossier table under the answer.
acceptance: Three parts in order: (1) assert measured origin where true so silence stops defaulting; (2) provenance travels with the observation, not the table; (3) simulation-origin evidence is excluded BEFORE ranking in operational mode and the exclusion is STATED. B06 passes with the simulated candidate's values transformed, and measured coverage is not inflated by simulated points. bldg1's wide sensor_data keeps its by-design mixed origin - labelled, never purged, never relabelled.
evidence: All three parts built, wired end to end and verified live. (1) 685 points declare ontosage:isSimulated false via scripts/declare_measured_origin.py, so silence stops defaulting to measured - graph now reads 685 measured / 1,409 simulated / 671 undeclared, against 0 / 1,408 / 1,356 before. (2) observation_provenance.py judges a reading, supporting a per-store measured_through boundary for an estate that needs one; this building declares none, by owner decision. (3) scorer.py takes `provenance` and `evidence_mode` and excludes simulated-origin candidates BEFORE ranking, stating the exclusion; plumbed through the discovery SPARQL, candidates, and the executor. CAUGHT THE LIVE INSTANCE R4 PREDICTED (BUG-515): a floor-3 ranking headed 'Best match: Room 3.27' whose noise, illuminance and occupancy were all SATURATE placeholders. Floor 3 holds 253 simulated and 150 undeclared instrumented points and zero measured. TWO DESIGN CORRECTIONS made after measuring: excluding anything NOT-measured emptied every ranking ('ranked 0, excluded 2' in bare fixtures), so it now excludes on a POSITIVE simulated verdict while unknowns rank but are not counted as measured coverage; and the first version of my own module overwrote the existing services/provenance.py, which was restored byte-identical from HEAD. OWNER DECISION 2026-09-12 closes the row: input/building.yaml declares provenance.evidence_policy: all_connected_readings, so bldg1 does not apply the exclusion - its synthetic points stand in for instruments to be connected later, and the origin is documented once in README.md. Verified live both ways: measured_only gives 'ranked 0, excluded 48 (48 for provenance)'; the declared policy returns 'Best match: Room 3.46 - Academic Office, score 0.5401'. R4 IS ACCEPTED, NOT RESOLVED, and docs/V12_SUPPORTED_SCOPE.md and the README both say so. A supervised pilot flips one key.

title: Typed retrieval outcomes - the kinds of nothing stop collapsing
covers: V11-4 REV-T04 REV-A03 REV-A04 REV-A05 REV-A06 BUG-499 BUG-487
why: R3. An empty window, a missing reference, an unregistered store and a forbidden read are four different facts and today they narrate the same. BUG-475 and BUG-487 were point repairs on two lanes; the distinction is systemic.
acceptance: Seven internal states with authorised external wording each. A03: a removed store reference gives REFERENCE_MISSING, never physical absence. A04: an unregistered store gives a specific resolution failure with no substitute backend. A05/A06 keep the review's own qualification (C08): where the adapter has no series catalogue the honest state is UNKNOWN, not a guess in either direction. Each state is seeded deliberately, and neither the exception wrapper nor the response collector converts one into ordinary success.
evidence: orchestrator/services/retrieval_outcome.py — the seven states from review p.8, each with ONE authorised external wording, plus a SeriesResolution axis kept SEPARATE from the query result. That separation is the review's own C08 correction: an empty result does not establish that a series is missing, because without a series catalogue a store cannot tell a broken identifier from a quiet period, so the honest state is UNKNOWN rather than a guess in either direction. 18 tests. A03: a removed reference gives REFERENCE_MISSING and the wording says outright 'I am NOT telling you the sensor is absent'. A04: an unregistered store gives a named configuration failure recording that no substitute backend was used. A05/A06: the two zero-row cases produce DIFFERENT wording, which is the whole point - a taxonomy the reader cannot perceive has achieved nothing. Precedence is tested: an unreachable store says nothing about rows, and policy beats everything without leaking that the thing exists. `may_recommend_installation` is True for exactly one state, NOT_DECLARED, which makes BUG-475's sentence unreachable from the other six. WIRED into report_agent._no_data_narrative, the lane that produced BUG-475: it now classifies using facts it already had (sensor_count, zero rows) instead of issuing one generic text, so 'sensors identified, no rows' reads differently from 'nothing of that kind declared'. Still no LLM call and still no claim about the building. Three tests assert the lane CALLS it, because a module nothing calls is the V6-T10 failure. WHY PARTIAL: sql_agent is named in the acceptance and is not yet wired - it needs a series-catalogue probe to distinguish CONFIRMED from UNKNOWN, which is adapter work, and BUG-499 (a nonexistent room times out rather than declining) is a referent-gate fix that belongs with it.

title: The response-collection contract becomes a test (no repair)
why: R7 is already CLOSED - all 37 intents audited, zero uncollected. What is missing is the guard that fails when intent 38 arrives with no collector. Building the repair would be treating a historical defect as still open, which the review names as its own failure mode.
acceptance: B02: a test enumerates every intent in intent_definitions.yaml, resolves its bus key and asserts the key is read on the response path. Deleting one collector branch fails the test. No generic success-without-answer state survives.
evidence: tests/test_every_lane_is_collected.py, 5 tests. NO REPAIR, per the row's own reasoning - R7 was audited closed on 2026-09-09 with zero uncollected lanes, and building a repair would be treating a historical defect as still open, which the review names as its own failure mode. The guard DERIVES the mapping rather than keeping one: for each of the 37 intents in intent_definitions.yaml it finds the declared node_method, parses that method with ast for the intermediate_results keys it writes, and asserts at least one is read on the response path - covering both access styles, the direct .get("x") and the typed ctx.<attr> snapshot, since missing either would produce a false failure. 25 intents have a node_method; the other 12 are the data group and flow through the shared pipeline. 76 keys are read on the response path. It can fail: test_deleting_a_collector_branch_would_fail_this_test removes register_result from the read-set and asserts the lane then looks uncollected - a guard that cannot detect its own defect is the literal scanner reporting clean over two directories with fifteen literals outside its scope. FOUND WHILE WRITING IT: the report-intake family's answer travels on dialogue_response, and report_intake_result is METADATA read by evidence/assemble.py so a filed report is citeable (TODO-229). My first assertion demanded report_intake_result be collected on the response path; the natural fix for that failing test would have been to publish a metadata dict where prose belongs. The distinction is now written into the test.

title: Resolve the requested interval once; forbid every downstream re-derivation
why: R2 residual, review T05. BUG-478 headed a report 'Yesterday' and described today because the formatter re-derived the window the retriever had already resolved. That fix was a point repair on one lane. We take the review's invariant (resolve once, never reinterpret) and NOT its full request envelope, which would be the parallel framework it warns against.
acceptance: The resolved interval is carried on the state and a test proves no formatter re-derives it. A07 passes with the clock frozen and yesterday/today seeded to different values, with the expectation computed independently of the production query builder. A08 passes across midnight and a DST transition using the configured zone, not a hardcoded 24-hour subtraction.
evidence: orchestrator/services/requested_interval.py is now the ONE resolver; dialogue_agent re-exports calendar_day_bounds for its existing callers. Found and fixed BUG-517 (P1): the ARBITER hours table mapped BOTH 'yesterday' and 'today' to 24.0h and fetch.py turned either into utcnow()-24h with the END BOUND None -- a rolling window ending now, half of it today, in UTC against local stamps. BUG-183 updated, still OPEN: the deterministic half is rebuilt, the live re-ask is owed and the 279.5s timeout is untouched.

title: Count, aggregation and data-quality contracts
covers: REV-A09 REV-A10 REV-A12 CAVEAT-006 BUG-497 BUG-506 CAVEAT-513
why: A cap on an exhaustive query does not fail - it under-reports (BUG-479). CAVEAT-006's residual is the same disease: the sensor census lists a class beside its own subclasses ('Air Quality Sensor 523, CO2 Sensor 214, CO2 Level Sensor 208') as if they were disjoint.
acceptance: A09: the known total comes from the fixture's contents, never from asking the limited path to grade itself; a truncated result says so and an unknown total is not invented. A10: max, min and average each use their intended operation, asserted against an independently computed expectation. A12: duplicate, invalid and out-of-order rows produce recorded accepted/excluded counts. A nested census states that its categories overlap.
evidence: orchestrator/services/reading_quality.py + the report lane rewritten to group by SENSOR. Found three defects that all printed real-looking numbers: BUG-520 (every report named its OLDEST reading as the latest -- `vals[-1]` in a DESC-ordered lane), BUG-521 P1 (a narrow-table report averaged 900 ppm CO2 with 21.5 degC into avg=590.5), BUG-522 (filtered rows vanished uncounted). tests/test_counts_and_aggregates_mean_what_they_say.py -- 39 tests. A09 expectation is the fixture's 2,770 written out, never the capped path's own 1,000. A10 asserts row order changes no statistic and that avg is not the midpoint of the range. A12 counts duplicate / non-numeric / no-timestamp separately and records out-of-order WITHOUT treating it as an exclusion. Census overlap (CAVEAT-006 residual) measured per building via ontology_inventory.overlap_notes and wired into BOTH census renderers; CAVEAT-523 logged for its extra round trip.

title: A unit conversion contract
why: In no plan anywhere - found by the reconciliation sweep, not carried from one. An approved conversion must be explicit and an unsupported pairing must be refused, otherwise a number changes meaning silently between the store and the sentence. BUG-257 was one instance: a unit sat in the graph and never reached the answer.
acceptance: A11: compatible units convert with the conversion named in the evidence record; unknown or incompatible pairings are rejected rather than assumed.
evidence: Closed BY V12-09, which is where the row said it would be: units.aggregation_decision shipped with V12-04 and nothing imported it. report_agent now consults it before any cross-sensor aggregate and RECORDS the refusal (`_aggregate_across_sensors`) rather than acting on it silently; _extract_highlights renders it. Verified on the live-shaped fixture that caused BUG-521: ppm and degC are refused with 'these readings measure different quantities', ppm and ppm are permitted with the target unit named.

title: Shared labels and context switches
why: Two rooms can share a label across floors or buildings, and a follow-up that changes room must clear the inherited state rather than answer about the old one. BUG-118 was one instance of this class ('floor 2' matched every floor whose name contained the digit); the class itself has no test.
acceptance: A13: an ambiguous label is resolved from authorised context or clarified, never silently cross-selected across buildings. A14: incompatible inherited state is cleared on a context switch and the co-reference rewrite cannot carry a stale referent.
evidence: orchestrator/services/context_switch.py, reusing the existence gate's OWN detectors so the switch guard and the gate cannot disagree about a question's subject. BUG-524: the co-reference rewrite could swap the room the user named, and because the rewrite replaces the query everywhere downstream the existence gate could not catch it -- the swapped room exists. BUG-525: carried-forward analytics were injected into a turn about a different room. tests/test_a_changed_subject_clears_what_it_invalidates.py -- 33 tests, negatives outnumbering positives because 'now plot that' is why carry-forward exists. A13's cross-building half is prevented by construction and now PINNED: an AST check that all four resolver queries filter on the active namespace. Within-building ambiguity is real and out of this row's scope -- logged as BUG-526 with the shape of the fix and why it needs its own row.

title: Policy applies before disclosure, on every output channel and to more than one identity
why: B11. A policy applied to the text but not to the dossier or the chart is not applied. BUG-195 was exactly this: the sparql lane could answer a reading question with NO PDP chokepoint. And BUG-191's lesson governs the grader - it counted the '2' inside `bldg2` as a sensor reading, so refusals scored PASS and a run reported a spurious 39/39.
acceptance: An unauthorised room, a restricted occupancy detail and a derived sensitive output are each refused before disclosure, checked in text, chart, dossier AND export, with identities whose permitted scopes differ. The grader must not count a digit inside a building id as a reading.
evidence: orchestrator/services/disclosure_gate.py — a SEPARATE module from publication_gate.py because their failure directions are opposite and a single module with a fail_open= switch would put one flag between correct and catastrophic. The verification gate fails OPEN (a verifier outage must not become a total outage); the disclosure gate fails CLOSED (publishing is the irreversible half). It DECIDES nothing — the PDP owns that at its four consult chokepoints — it propagates a decision already made to the surfaces built from the refused lane: chart, export, evidence dossier and evidence record. Detection reads the `denied_by_policy` marker that enforcement.refusal_payload writes, never the prose: BUG-191's grader counted the '2' inside bldg2 as a reading, and a gate guessing from wording would repeat that with worse consequences. Wired into _response_node BEFORE the publication gate, since that gate rewrites final_response wholesale. tests/test_a_policy_governs_every_channel.py — 25 tests including the >1-identity case (two identities diverge because their VERDICTS differ; the gate reads no role of its own, asserted by a source check) and a test whose only job is to make a future merge of the two gates fail loudly. The grader half of the acceptance was already satisfied: scripts/leak_benchmark.py carries BUG-191's word-boundary fix and counts per-space detail rather than digits. LIVE RE-ASK OWED on a denied turn that would otherwise have produced a chart.

title: A lane function returns what it declares, and present data is recognised as present
why: A01 is not hypothetical here. BUG-476 was `_standardize_results` with NO return statement, so every planned query silently lost its SPARQL results and the pipeline treated None as an empty answer. A02 is BUG-152's shape: a declared sensor with a working reference and rows was answered with a canned denial.
acceptance: A01: with two matching sensors the list function returns the exact declared identifiers and its declared type; an unexpected None fails loudly INTERNALLY rather than becoming an empty answer. A02: presence and data are recognised, with no claim that installation is required.
evidence: A01 was ALREADY covered - test_no_annotated_function_can_return_none_by_accident existed from BUG-476's fix - so the work was the guard's own accuracy and scope, not a new framework. Its _falls_off_the_end was wrong in both directions: it treated ANY trailing `if` as terminating, so a function ending `if hit: return hit` with no else - the BUG-476 shape exactly - was invisible to the check written to catch it; and its Try arm asked whether ANY tail returned when one returning handler does not stop another falling through. Replaced with a recursive _terminates() covering If (needs a non-empty else, both branches terminating), Try (all handlers plus a returning finally), With, Match and While (only `while True` with no break). Six unit tests pin the ANALYSER, because the sweep only reports a number and neither error was visible from that number. Scope widened from orchestrator/ alone to orchestrator/ + shared/ - 3,920 lines including the config every service reads. Result: 1,642 + 67 annotated functions, shared/ clean, and ONE real offender the old guard could not see (BUG-511, DocumentBuilder.render, latent - unreachable only because of a guard forty lines away). A02 delivered as tests/test_lane_return_contracts.py, 13 tests: the readings and the declared sensor are found IN THE SHAPE THE LANES PRODUCE (the BUG-477 trap), the store reference survives, and with rows present the empty-result branch is unreachable so none of BUG-475's eight claims can be produced. The existing coverage of that half was a single source-text assertion that would have passed even if the recogniser stopped finding rows. A cross-check keeps the two forbidden-claim lists from drifting apart.

title: Adapter parity, and a version/snapshot policy
why: TODO-143 ran the Timescale and Cassandra adapters once, against real servers. The review is explicit that a mock alone does not establish adapter compatibility. And a graph revision that changes between discovery and retrieval produces a mixed result nobody can explain.
acceptance: A15: equivalent seeded data returns equivalent semantic results AND equivalent evidence through each supported wide/narrow adapter, against real servers. A16: the defined snapshot policy prevents an unexplained mixed result when a mapping changes mid-turn.
evidence: A15 PROVEN AGAINST REAL SERVERS, not mocks -- which is the review's own point and TODO-143's lesson. TimescaleDB and Cassandra started from docker-compose.timeseries-backends.yml and seeded with 25 sensors x 192 readings each (2 days @ 15 min, 4,800 rows per store, hypertable confirmed via timescaledb_information.hypertables). The SAME logical series through a SQL hypertable and a CQL table partitioned by sensor gives identical count/min/max/mean AND identical latest timestamp + value. Evidence is asserted SEPARATELY from the statistics because two stores can agree on every number and disagree about which reading is newest, and 'when was this true' is a recommendation's expiry date. Row limit and newest-first ordering pinned for both. A16: orchestrator/services/graph_snapshot.py pins the uuid->store mapping at DISCOVERY and re-compares at response time; a moved sensor is NAMED and the turn never retries, because a retry answers from the new mapping and says nothing about the old one. Honest about its limits: the statement-count fingerprint cannot see an equal-count replace and the module says so rather than being trusted for it. Found BUG-532 (all seven adapters' validate_query crashed on `.upper()` when handed the None that build_timeseries_query returns) and BUG-533 (two live tests pinned to a uuid from one seed run). tests/test_adapter_parity_and_snapshot.py -- 27 tests; test_timescale_cassandra_adapters.py 26 (was 24 + 2 failing).
notes: Three of my own source-text guards fired on PROSE rather than code during this row -- see lessons.md #102. The surviving one strips comments before scanning. Registry entries from the seeder NOT committed (BUG-541).

title: The cache cannot outlive the authorisation that produced it
why: resp_cache holds an answer for an hour. If it can be served to an identity whose permitted scope differs from the one that filled it, the permission check is decorative. B12 applies precisely because a cache exists.
acceptance: B12: a cached answer cannot bypass the current authorisation or provenance policy; the cache key carries the authorised scope, and a test proves a narrower identity misses rather than hits.
evidence: The cache partition now carries the REVISION as well as the identity: {building_id}|{role[:user_id]}|r{revision}. BUILD_SHA where the image has one; process boot time otherwise, which is correct here because /app/orchestrator is bind-mounted so a restart IS a deployment - and that is the case BUG-498 recorded, where a guard was fixed, the orchestrator restarted, and the pre-fix answer was still served at 0.9s from cache. Chosen as a KEY COMPONENT rather than another flush: policy_admin.invalidate_policy_caches already flushes on a policy edit and is kept, because editing a policy does not change the code revision - but a flush is wrapped in try/except and fails OPEN, while a key fails CLOSED. Revision sits LAST so the partition-blind {building_id}|* sweep still reaches everything. 10 tests: a narrower identity MISSES rather than hits (B12's explicit requirement), two occupants do not share a partition while two facility managers deliberately do, an entry from another revision is unreachable, the revision is never the literal 'unknown' that BUILD_SHA actually holds here, the sweep still matches, and the policy flush is still wired. OWED: no live model this session, so the round trip - cache an answer, restart, confirm it is not served - is proved by key comparison but not end to end.

title: Failure, timeout and partial completion become typed outcomes
why: CAVEAT-415 is PARTIALLY_FIXED: 62 failures in six hours logged an empty message and hid an 11% silent quality drop. The review's rule is that a retry which succeeds is still a first-pass failure and must stay separately visible.
acceptance: B15: an injected lane timeout, backend outage and delayed completion each produce an explicit partial or failure outcome; first-pass and retry status remain separately reportable everywhere a number is published.
evidence: orchestrator/services/turn_outcome.py. `_safe_node` caught every exception as one undifferentiated Exception and recorded `{node}_error: str(e)` -- so a TIMEOUT, an unreachable BACKEND and a raised DEFECT were one fact, and on a message-less exception (httpx.ReadTimeout, asyncio.TimeoutError, bare Exception()) `str(e)` is the EMPTY STRING, so the record was not merely untyped but blank. Five typed outcomes now, classified by walking the CAUSE CHAIN (a timeout wrapped by a helper is still a timeout) and matched by class NAME so the classifier imports no transport. TIMEOUT is its own type because of CAVEAT-500: the same question measured 10.7s / 61.1s / 13.3s, every answer correct -- folding latency in with failure makes a run unreadable in both directions. FIRST_PASS is decided where the outcome is RECORDED, not re-derived by whoever publishes a number, and a turn that recovered on retry has outcome=OK with first_pass_ok=False. Successes are recorded too: without the denominator '3 lanes timed out' cannot be told apart from '3 of 3' and '3 of 40'. CAVEAT-415's other half closed at the LOGGER rather than at 871 bare `{e}` call sites: a filter on get_logger() annotates any WARNING+ whose formatted message ends in a colon, so an empty failure line is impossible including in code not yet written. tests/test_a_failure_says_which_kind_it_was.py -- 20 tests.

Kept here only as context: _TRACE_STAGE_MARKERS now names the real keys, and only a real turn shows the plan_trace actually listing sparql/sql/analytics as having run. This row already exercises how a turn's execution is recorded, and needs live turns anyway, so the check rides with it rather than inventing a row for one assertion. Two of my own checks were wrong first: the test's stand-in classes were named _ReadTimeout/_ConnectError and did not match (the name contract working as designed), and the `str(e)` guard fired on the wrapper's own COMMENT explaining why str(e) was wrong. title: ECA fixtures, and a rule that states its scope
why: BUG-482: a concept-triggered rule evaluates ONE point of however many carry the class and reads as if it covers them all - temperature_reading currently binds to the outside weather feed. The engine now logs which point it chose, which is honesty about the defect rather than the fix.
acceptance: B03: a positive fixture matches and a negative fixture does not, with NO actuation required or implied - the review is explicit that a rule firing in a test should mean its condition matched, not that equipment moved. The engine stays notify-only for Gate A. A rule either evaluates every matching point or must declare a scope.
evidence: BUG-482 closed by making the rule SAY what it watches rather than by guessing for it. RuleTrigger gained `scope: all | first_reporting` with NO DEFAULT: a concept rule declaring neither is loaded DISABLED with a message naming both options. Either default would have silently picked a meaning the author did not -- and `first_reporting` as a default is exactly the behaviour that made this a defect. `scope: all` evaluates EVERY matching point; breach duration and cooldown were already keyed by (rule_id, uuid), so per-point evaluation needed no new state -- the machinery was there and one point was ever put through it. A point with no value is EXCLUDED rather than counted as non-breaching: 'no reading' is not 'within threshold'. tests/test_eca_fixtures.py -- 19 tests: positive, negative, both threshold boundaries, all six operators, the three scope behaviours, and notify-only asserted FROM THE SOURCE (no actuation_registry / actuate( / write_point), so the day an actuate action type appears these fixtures fail instead of quietly meaning something else.
notes: The shipped rule declares `first_reporting`, NOT `all`, deliberately: it is named humidity_damp_floor3 and a concept trigger has no spatial qualifier (TODO-528), so `all` would notify about every floor under a rule whose name promises one -- a worse lie than the one being fixed.
